The brief contents of the petition are as under:
On 03052020, at about 08.30 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing SCCH-10 reg.No.KA44S4331 as a pillion rider and the same was ridden by its rider by name Shivananjaiah and when they reached near Mavinakere - Mayasandra Main Road, at that time, the rider of the Bajaj Pulsar Motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16EM1920 ridden the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result, the petitioner fell down from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries and rider of their motorcycle by name Shivananjaia died on the spot.

3. Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital and research center,
B.G.Nagar, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandaya District, wherein she has taken treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery and again she admitted in People Tree hospital for further treatment.
The petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/ SCCH-10 towards medical expenses.
The petitioner was advised to take followup treatment and in this regard the petitioner is still taking followup treatment.

Further at the time of accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 50 years,
working as an Agriculturist and earning Rs.15,000/p.m., and was unable to do work as earlier to the accident.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ from the respondents under all heads together with interest and costs.
4. In response to the court notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their respective counsel and filed their written statement.

5. The brief contentions of the respondent No.1 are as under:
This respondent has denied the issuance of policy SCCH-10 to the alleged vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
The owner has not complied the Sec.134 (c) of M.V.Act.

Further contended that, at the time of accident the rider of the alleged motorcycle was not having valid and effective driving license to ridden the motorcycle and the respondent No.2 has violated the policy terms and conditions of the policy.
The respondent claim right U/Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
The respondent No.2 has denied the manner of accident.

The brief contentions of the respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 has admitted that she is the owner of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16EM1920.

Further contended that, the accident was not occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle, on the other hand, the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44S4331.
Further this respondent has denied the age, occupation and SCCH-10 income of the petitioner and medical expenses incurred by her.

Further the respondent No.2 has admitted that, she is the owner of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16 EM1920 and the same was insured with the respondent No.1 under policy No.472108/31/2019/10569 covering for the period from to 12032019 to 11032024.
Since the insurance policy of the said motorcycle is covering the risk of this respondent/owner and the insurance company has no Indemnify the risk of insurer on any award to be passed against him.

Hence,
on all these contentions, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2.
7.

On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 0305 2020 at about 8.30 p.m., while the petitioner was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44S4331 as a pillion SCCH-10 rider and the same was ridden by her husband i.e., deceased Shivananjaiah and when she reached near Mavinakere Mayasandra Main Road, at that time, the rider of the Bajaj Pulsar Motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA16EM1920 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner, as a result the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award?

R E A S O N S 12. ISSUE NO.1: The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/
with respect to the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident.
To prove the accident and the accident was occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing reg. No.KA16 EM1920.
The petitioner herself got examined as PW1 and produced the documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.

The Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint,
Ex.P.3 is SCCH-10 the charge sheet, Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.7 is the wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is the medical bills, Ex.P.9 is the prescriptions and Ex.P.10 is the Xray.
13. The respondent No.1 and 2 have disputed the accident as the accident was occurred on the negligence of rider of the offending motorcycle.

The respondent No.1 contended that, the deceased i.e., rider of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44S4331 has ridden his motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and without observing the vehicles on main road, thereby he dashed his motorcycle to the offending motorcycle and caused the accident.
14. To prove the defence, the official of the respondent No.1 company got examined as RW1 and produced the documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.8.

After the accident the case was registered against SCCH-10 the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA 16EM1920 and the police have investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle for the offence punishable under section 279, 338,
304(A) of IPC and Sec.181 of M.V.Act.
The petitioner also produced the spot mahazar, IMV report and wound certificate as per Ex.P.4, 5 and Ex.P.7.

Though the respondent No.1/insurance company contended that, there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle, but no material is produced before the court to substantiate their contention except to show the police have filed the charge sheet for the offence punishable U/Sec.181 of M.V.Act as the rider of the offending motorcycle had violated the Sec.3 and 4 of M.V.Act as there is no DL to the rider of the offending motorcycle.

4 15.

Though the respondent no.1 has cross examined the PW1, but nothing has been elicited from SCCH-10 the mouth of the petitioner/Pw1 to show the accident was occurred on the negligence of rider of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44S4331.

Therefore in view of the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, I am of the opinion that, the accident was occurred on sole negligence of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16EM 1920.
Hence, I answer the issue No.1 in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
This petition is filed for seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident as stated above.

The specific contention of the petitioner that, she was proceeding on motorcycle as a pillion rider and when they reached near Mavinakere - Mayasandra Main road, at that time, the rider of the Bajaj Pulsor motorcycle bearing KA16EM1920 ridden the same in rash and SCCH-10 negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle, as a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injury.

Immediately she was shifted to the Adichunchanagiri hospital, B.G.Nagar, and she has treatment in the said hospital and underwent surgery and again admitted in People tree hospital for further treatment.
Therefore the petitioner become disabled and lost her earning capacity.
17. In this case, the petitioner has proved the accident and injuries sustained by her in the alleged accident by producing cogent evidence.
Further the petitioner got examined the doctor and MRO as PW2 and PW3 and produced the documents as per Ex.P.11 to 18.

The Ex.P.11 is the Clinical notes,
Ex.P.12 is the Xray, Ex.P.13 is the authorization letter, Ex.P.14 is the accident register, Ex.P.15 is the Police intimation, Ex.P.16 is the outpatient records, Ex.P.17 is the case sheet and Ex.P.18 is the Xray.
SCCH-10 18.
The respondents have not disputed the treatment taken by the petitioner.
The PW2 has assessed the disability of the petitioner and the PW2 is not a treated doctor.

The doctor stated that,
the petitioner has sustained L1 compression fracture with no Neurological deficits and fracture of left proximal and distal phalanx.
The Pw2 admitted that the fractures are united and the petitioner can do agriculture work and PW2 denied that, he has assessed the exorbitant disability to help the petitioner.

19. The Pw2 has assessed the disability of the petitioner and also gave evidence with respect to the disability of the petitioner for L1 compression fracture with no Neurological deficits and fracture of left proximal and distal phalanx as 15% for Thoracic and Thoracolumbar spine injuries.
The Pw 2/doctor has not opined the disability for limb and to whole body.
The SCCH-10 wound certificate and discharge summaries as per Ex.P.7 and 17 case sheet disclose the injury and treatment.

So, in view of all these circumstances, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following different heads:
20. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON THE ACCOUNT OF DISABILITY.

Therefore the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
21. At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision of Yashoda.H and others V/s. Sharath Kumar Achar and another.

Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 03052020 Therefore, Rs.14,500/ has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

22. So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that, at the time of accident,
he was aged about 50 years.
To prove the age, the petitioner has produced the Aadhar card as per Ex.P.6 it discloses the date of birth year of the petitioner as 1971.
Hence the same is considered as date of birth year of the petitioner.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is 49 years at the time of accident.

Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is "13".
23.
The petitioner claims that, she was working as an Agriculturist and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ p.m. and due to accidental injury she is unable to do work.
The petitioner also gave oral evidence and deposed SCCH-10 before the court that, she is unable to do his work as which he was doing earlier.
The doctor/Pw2 stated that, the petitioner has sustained L1 compression fracture with no Neurological deficits and fracture of left proximal and distal phalanx injuries.
The PW2 has assessed the disability to the petitioner as 15%.

The PW2 has stated in his evidence that, the petitioner can do agriculture work, therefore the disability assessed by the doctor/ Pw2 as 15%
cannot affected to the petitioner as her functional disability to the extent of 15%.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that, the functional disability of the petitioner is to be taken as 9% against 15%.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.2,03,580/ (Rs.14,500 X 2 X 13 X 9/100)
towards loss of future income on the account of disability of the petitioner.

24. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
SCCH-10

As per the Wound certificate and case sheet as per Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.17, the petitioner has sustained L1 compression fracture with no Neurological deficits and fracture of left proximal and distal phalanx injury.
As petitioner has undergone pain and sufferings due to injuries sustained in the accident.

By considering the above facts and discussion made above and looking to the nature of injuries, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.30,000/ under the head of Pain and sufferings.
25. LOSS OF AMENITIES
Further on perusal of evidence of PW1, it reveals that, petitioner has sustained injury and the same is mentioned above paras.
The petitioner was aged about 49 years at the time of accident.

Considering the above facts and on perusal of evidence of PW1 and 2,
considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I deem it just and reasonable to grant Smt.Maniyamma vs The Oriental Insurance on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3001741/
6 for SCCH-10 compensation of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of amenities.
26. ATTENDANT, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
Further on perusal of ExP17 i.e., case sheet produced by the Pw3, it discloses that, the petitioner has taken treatment in Adichunchanagiri hospital from 0305 2020 to 08052020 i.e., for a period of 06 days she has taken treatment as an inpatient.
Looking to the period of hospitalization, naturally she was unable to do her own work and she was needed help from some other person.
The attendance and nourishment charges of the petitioner during the hospitalization is required.
Therefore it is proper to award the amount of Rs.6,000/ under the head of attendant, food and nourishment and conveyance charges.
27. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD SCCH-10 AND REST PERIOD:

Further due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner might have taken rest at least for a period of 1 month as she was sustained L1 compression fracture with no Neurological deficits and fracture of left proximal and distal phalanx injury and as such, if 1 month income is awarded under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period, certainly it would meet the ends of justice.
For the above reason, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.14,500/under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
28. MEDICAL EXPENSES
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner has got marked the medical bills and prescriptions as per Ex.P.8 and Ex.P.9.
The petitioner has contended that, she has made expenses towards medical expenses.
As per calculation memo for the medical bill as per Ex.P.8 the total bill is of SCCH-10 Rs.24,539/.
The respondents have not at all disputed the claim of the petitioner with respect to the medical bills except denial.
Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, I proceed to award Rs.24,539/ under the head of medical expenses.

29. By considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reasons, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,98,619/ under the following heads:

 account of disability 2.

4.Towards attendant, food and Rs. 6,000/
nourishment and conveyance charges 5.

laid up period and rest period.

LIABILITY:
On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of objection statement, it reveals that, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and the respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending motorcycle.

Further, as stated above that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16EM1920 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

31. The respondent No.1 contended that, the police have filed the charge sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16EM1920 for offence punishable under section 279, 338, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.181 of M.V.Act as the rider of the motorcycle had not driving license at the time of accident.
The respondent No.1 contended that, the rider of the offending motorcycle SCCH-10 had not driving license, therefore there is a breach of policy conditions.
Therefore the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
32. To support of it the insurance company has lead the evidence of its official as RW1 and produced the documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.8.

The Ex.R.1 is the authorization letter, Ex.R.2 is the policy copy, Ex.R.3 is the copy of notice, Ex.R.4 is the copy of acknowledgement, Ex.R.5 is the notice u/s.133 of M.V.Act issued by the police to the owner of offending vehicle, Ex.R.6 is the copy of reply notice issued by the owner, Ex.R.7 is the copy notice u/s.133 of M.V.Act to the owner of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44S4331 and Ex.R.8 is the reply.

On perusal of the Ex.R.6 and Ex.R.8 i.e., reply notice issued by the owners of the motorcycle to the notice U/s.133 have stated that, the rider of the offending motorcycle and the rider of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44S4331 have not Driving license at the time SCCH-10 of accident.

The petitioner has relied the decision reported in 2018 (1) SCC 750 between Dinesh Kumar.J V/s.
National Insurance Co, wherein it was held: "Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Ss.166 and 173 - Compensation - Contributory negligence - Driving vehicle without licence -Whether can by itself amount to contributory negligence."

Dinesh Kumar.J V/s.
National Insurance Co
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Another decision reported in 2019 ACJ 42 between Saraswathi Palariya and others V/s. New Indian Assurance Co.Ltd., and others, wherein it was held that:
"Negligence - Contributory negligence - Driving License - High Court fixed contributory negligence on the deceased on the ground that deceased was driving the vehicle without a driving licence - Held :
driving without a driving licence may expose the person to other liabilities but no inference of contributory negligence can be drawn on SCCH-10 that basis.

entities.text: Saraswathi Palariya and others V/s. New Indian Assurance Co.Ltd., and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In these two decision, the Hon'ble Apex court clearly held that though the deceased had not Driving License itself is not a ground to inference contributory negligence.

Smt.Maniyamma vs The Oriental Insurance on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3001741/
8

Therefore in this case the respondents have not placed any material to show there is a contributory negligence in the accident by the rider of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA 44S4331 except he has not Driving License.
The non having DL itself is not a ground to contributory negligence, unless proved the contributory negligence.

In this case the respondents have not proved the contributory negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44S4331.
33.
The respondents argued that, the offending motorcycle rider also not having Driving License.
The Ex.R.6 is the reply issued by the owner of the offending motorcycle, clearly stated that the rider of the offending motorcycle had not driving license at the time of accident.
SCCH-10

The counsel for the petitioner argued that, though the rider of the motorcycle has not Driving license, but the policy was in force, therefore the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation as they had indemnify to the insured and relied the decisions reported in AIR 2018 SC 592 between Pappu and others V/s. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another, wherein held that:/
"Motor Vehicles Act (59 of 1988), S.149 - Insurer's liability - Accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of truck -Insurer taking plea that driver of offending truck had no valid licence - Except copy of driving licence of person,
owner of offending truck not producing any evidence establishing that it was driven by authorized person having valid driving license - Fact that offending truck was duly insured - Would not per se make insurance company directed to pay award amount to claimants in first instance and in turn,
recover same from owner of vehicle.

Another decision of Singh Ram V/s. Nirmala and SCCH-10 others in Civil Appeal No.2103/2018 dated 06032018, in this case the Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the direction issued by the Tribunal for pay and recovery order cannot be faulted.

entities.text: Singh Ram V/s. Nirmala and SCCH-10 others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision and discussions, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that, where the driver did not possess a driving license and there is a breach of policy conditions.
In this case the petitioner is the third party claimant.

Therefore in view of violation of policy conditions, the liability has to be sladded on owner of the vehicle, but in view of the policy to the motorcycle by respondent No.2 though rider of the motorcycle had not valid effective driving licence, at the time of accident, but in view of policy and indemnify of the insurer to the owner, the insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the third party injured and insurer has right to recover the same from the owner as a petitioner is a third party.
SCCH-10 Hence the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of alleged motorcycle is liable to pay compensation of Rs.2,98,619/ with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit and recover the same from the owner/respondent No.2.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.

However, the respondent No.1 being insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order and recover the same from the owner/ respondent No.2.
